notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed. The upstream package was not importable where the gate ran (it needs Python 3.11 or newer, MuJoCo, numpy and the model assets), so the fake backend is this package's pure Python kinematic FetchSlide stand-in (fake.py) and was never compared with the upstream environment; the sim backend (gymnasium.make of FetchSlide-v4) was not run. Warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1, which is bookkeeping in the bridge and makes no native call; four G8.NO_UNIT for integer/numeric inputs the bridge derives (ticks, seed twice, action.values); five G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space, reset, step and close, because the upstream class hierarchy is built by the call get_base_fetch_env(MujocoRobotEnv), which the gate's AST reader cannot follow, while every name occurs in the clone (robot_env.py:87-88, :114, :154, :327). The fake models the documented position control (0.05 scaling), the start and target sampling and the 50-step truncation, but not MuJoCo contacts, friction, actuators or sensors; its fidelity gaps say so. No hardware is attached or claimed; this is a simulated R0 device with no operator-required limit and no site-limits overlay. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
